rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps
rows.expected_answer: You choose the order and the best answer is 6. Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer:
You choose the order. Timestamps have nothing to do with it. Apply **Hardened Scales** first and then **Doubling Season**, and **Walking Ballista** enters with 6 counters: (2+1)×2. In the other order you'd get 2×2+1 = 5.

Why: both are replacement effects ("instead", per `614.1a`). Ballista's "enters with X +1/+1 counters" also counts as a replacement effect under `614.1c`. When two or more replacement effects try to modify the same event, the affected object's controller picks one to apply (`616.1`). Here that's you. Neither of your two effects is a self-replacement effect or any of the other special cases in `616.1a`–`d`, so `616.1e` lets you pick either one. After that one is applied, the process repeats with whatever still applies (`616.1f`). Each effect gets only one chance to modify the event (`614.5`).

The Scryfall rulings say the same thing. Both cards apply to a permanent entering with counters: "Doubling Season affects permanents that enter with counters." On ordering, the Hardened Scales ruling says: "you choose the order to apply those effects, no matter who controls the sources of those effects."

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer:
No Tron mana. While **Blood Moon** is on the battlefield, each of your Urza's lands is just a Mountain that taps for {R}. You get 3 red mana in total, not 7 colorless. **Urza's Tower** can't tap for {C}{C}{C}, and it can't even tap for {C}.

Blood Moon says "Nonbasic lands are Mountains." That is a type-changing effect, which applies in layer 4 (613.1d). It sets each land's land subtype. Per 205.1a, when an effect sets an object's subtypes, the new subtype replaces the old ones. So your lands lose Urza's, Tower, Mine and Power-Plant. Blood Moon's Scryfall ruling confirms this: "Nonbasic lands will lose any other land types and abilities they had. They will gain the land type Mountain and gain the ability "{T}: Add {R}.""

There are two separate problems:
1. The lands no longer have their printed "{T}: Add {C}. If you control..." abilities at all.
2. Even if they did, those abilities check land types, not card names. Nothing you control is an Urza's Mine, Power-Plant or Tower any more.

The names don't change and the lands don't become basic. They're still nonbasic Mountains named Urza's Tower and so on. If Blood Moon leaves the battlefield, they work normally again.

rows.question: follow up: what if I play [[Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth]] AFTER the moon is already down? urborg has the later timestamp so shouldn't it make everything a Swamp too? my friend says no
rows.expected_answer: Your friend is right. Both effects are layer 4 type-changing effects (613.1d). Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). Urborg is just a Mountain with '{T}: Add {R}' and nothing becomes a Swamp. (Any actual basic Swamps you control are still Swamps because Blood Moon only affects nonbasic lands.)

outcome.answer:
Your friend is right. Even if **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** comes down after **Blood Moon**, nothing becomes a Swamp. The order you played them in doesn't matter.

Urborg is a nonbasic land, so **Blood Moon** ("Nonbasic lands are Mountains.") applies to it. Both effects change types, so both apply in layer 4 (`613.1d`). Timestamps usually decide the order within a layer (`613.7`), but per `613.8` dependency overrides timestamps. Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's, because applying Blood Moon changes whether Urborg's effect exists at all (`613.8a`). Under `305.7`, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type "loses all abilities generated from its rules text". A dependent effect waits until the effect it depends on has been applied (`613.8b`). So Blood Moon applies first, Urborg loses "Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types.", and that effect never applies.

The official ruling covers this exact case: Urborg "won't turn lands into Swamps, no matter in what order those effects started to apply." Urborg ends up as a legendary Mountain that only taps for {R}.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is a regular **Tarmogoyf**. It doesn't get your two +1/+1 counters or the +3/+3 from **Giant Growth**. It does copy Goyf's power/toughness ability, so it knows exactly how big it should be: the same base size as yours.

Per `707.2`, a copy takes only the copiable values, meaning what's printed on the card (including rules text and power/toughness). "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." The Clone ruling says the same thing: it doesn't copy counters or "any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness". So the +1/+1 counters and the Giant Growth stay with your Goyf only.

On the */*+1 part: Goyf's size comes from its rules text, "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1." Per `707.2a`, a copy gets the abilities of the object it copies because those come from its rules text. The Clone therefore has that same ability and counts the same graveyards. If there are 4 card types among cards in all graveyards, their Clone-Goyf is 4/5. Yours is 4/5 + 2 counters + 3, so 9/10 until end of turn. Once Giant Growth goes to the graveyard, it can add instant to the count, which pumps both Goyfs equally. (Compare the Quicksilver Gargantuan example in `707.9d`: a copy loses Goyf's ability only when the copy effect sets its own P/T, which Clone doesn't.)

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
With **Humility** out first and **Opalescence** arriving later, your non-enchantment creatures are still 1/1 with no abilities. Humility itself becomes a 4/4 creature with no abilities. Opalescence is not a creature at all: it says "Each *other* non-Aura enchantment", so it never animates itself. If Opalescence was out first, everything flips: Humility is a 1/1 and so is every other creature.

Here's how the layers work out:
- **Layer 4:** Opalescence makes Humility (and any other non-Aura enchantment) a creature.
- **Layer 6:** Humility now removes all abilities from creatures, including its own. Per `613.6`, once an effect starts to apply, it keeps applying "even if the ability generating the effect is removed during this process." So Humility's 1/1 effect still applies in layer 7b.
- **Layer 7b:** Both effects set base P/T here (`613.4b`), so they apply in timestamp order. The earlier one goes first and the later one overwrites it (`613.7`). A static ability's effect has its object's timestamp (`613.7a`), and an object gets its timestamp when it enters (`613.7d`).

**Humility older (your case):** Humility's 1/1 applies first. Then Opalescence sets Humility to 4/4, because its mana value is 4. Your regular creatures stay 1/1, since Opalescence only affects enchantments. Any other animated enchantment ends up with P/T equal to its mana value.

**Opalescence older:** Opalescence's P/T effect applies first, then Humility makes every creature 1/1, Humility included. The official ruling walks through exactly this: "Layer 7b: Humility becomes 4/4 and Worship becomes 4/4. (Opalescence). Humility becomes 1/1 and Worship becomes 1/1 (Humility)."

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes, you can cast **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** straight from your hand for {5}{B}{R}. With a modal double-faced card, you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack (712.11b), and only that face is checked to see whether it can be cast (712.11c).

In your library, graveyard or any other zone besides the battlefield and stack, it's **not** a planeswalker card. It has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it's a creature card (Valki) with mana value 2.

That doesn't matter for your two examples, because both only look at the battlefield. On the battlefield, a modal DFC has only the characteristics of the face that's up (712.8f). So Tibalt on the battlefield is a planeswalker. **Vraska's Contempt** can target it, and **Kaya's Ghostform** ("Enchant creature or planeswalker you control") can enchant it.

One catch with Ghostform: when Tibalt dies or is exiled, the card comes back with its front face up, because a DFC put onto the battlefield from anywhere other than the stack enters front face up (712.14). So you get **Valki** back, not Tibalt. Valki's enters trigger will then happen.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer:
No, it doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would get priority (704.3), and they "pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability" (704.4). If the creature drops to 0 toughness partway through a resolution and is back above 0 when that resolution ends, 704.5f never sees it at 0. The 704.4 example is exactly this case: Maro sits at toughness 0 mid-resolution and survives. The **Maro** ruling agrees that if the toughness "goes back up above 0 before the end of that announcement or resolution, it won't be put into your graveyard." If it's still at 0 or less when the spell finishes, it does die.

You can't respond between the two **Ragavan**s. The legend rule is a state-based action (704.5j), and SBAs "don't use the stack" (704.1). They are "dealt with before a player would receive priority" (117.2d). So as soon as the second Ragavan is on the battlefield, before anyone gets priority again, you choose which one to keep and the other goes to your graveyard. Nobody gets a window in between. You can still use the one you lose for things that happen with no priority needed, such as abilities that trigger when it dies or leaves the battlefield. Those go on the stack after the SBA check (704.3).

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?
rows.expected_answer: 1) Yes. Color identity includes mana symbols in the mana cost AND in the rules text (903.4), so Kenrith's identity is WUBRG even though his mana cost is only {4}{W}. Nicol Bolas, the Ravager (UBR) is legal because every color in its identity is in Kenrith's (903.5c). 2) Yes, Kenrith can go to the command zone. If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead - a replacement effect (903.9b). Graveyard/exile use a separate state-based action (903.9a). Either way it's optional.

outcome.answer:
1) Yes, you can run **Nicol Bolas, the Ravager**. 2) You can choose: **Kenrith** can go to the command zone instead of your hand, or you can leave him in your hand. The command-zone option covers hand and library, not only graveyard and exile.

**Color identity:** Per `903.4`, a card's color identity includes the mana symbols in its mana cost *and* its rules text. Kenrith's abilities use {R}, {G}, {W}, {U} and {B}, so his identity is all five colors. Bolas's front face costs {1}{U}{B}{R}. Per `903.4d`, his back face also counts, and its color indicator is blue, black and red. Under `903.5c`, every color in a card's identity has to be in your commander's identity, and Bolas's are.

**Unsummon:** Per `903.9b`, "If a commander would be put into its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead." This replacement happens as **Unsummon** resolves, and it's optional. The graveyard/exile option (`903.9a`) is a separate rule. If you keep Kenrith in hand and cast him from there, no commander tax applies. Per `903.8`, tax only applies to casts from the command zone, and only those casts add to the tax.

rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. Fling damage is noncombat, so it never counts toward the 21 either; it just reduces your life total normally.

outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose. The Clone isn't her commander, so its 6 damage doesn't count toward the 21. Per 903.10a you lose only to "21 or more combat damage by the same commander". Commander status belongs to the physical card, not to anything copying it: per 903.3 "A permanent that's copying a commander... is not a commander." So the **Clone** copying **Rafiq of the Many** is a separate, non-commander source. Its 6 damage still lowers your life total as normal (119.2), but your commander-damage tally from Rafiq stays at 15.

Fling doesn't count either. 903.10a counts only combat damage. If she sacrifices Rafiq to **Fling**, that damage is noncombat: it comes off your life total but adds nothing to the 21. The same goes for any noncombat damage Rafiq deals itself.

One thing to watch: if Rafiq attacks alone, its own triggers give it +1/+1 and double strike ("Whenever a creature you control attacks alone, it gains double strike until end of turn"). Rafiq is a 3/3, so attacking alone it would be at least 4/4 hitting twice, which is 8 or more combat damage and enough to take you from 15 past 21 in one swing. If the Clone is also on the battlefield, its exalted copy adds another +1/+1.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
rows.expected_answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana added during your upkeep is lost before your main phase (106.4). Tap the lands in your main phase instead. 2) Yes. Casting a spell includes a step where, if the total cost includes mana, you get a chance to activate mana abilities such as tapping lands (601.2g), and only then do you pay the total cost (601.2h). You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

outcome.answer:
1) No. Mana you add during your upkeep doesn't last until your main phase. Per `106.4`, "Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, and the player is said to lose this mana." When the upkeep ends, that mana is gone before you reach your main phase. To cast **Jace, the Mind Sculptor**, tap your lands in the main phase.

2) Yes, you can tap lands partway through casting it, and you don't need to float mana first. Tapping a land for mana is activating a mana ability (`106.12`). Per `605.3a`, you can activate one "whenever you are casting a spell or activating an ability that requires a mana payment." Casting has a set step for this. Per `601.2g`, once the total cost is set, you "have a chance to activate mana abilities," and that has to happen before you pay costs in `601.2h`. So the usual order is: put **Snapcaster Mage** on the stack, lock in its cost, tap lands, then pay. Floating mana first also works, as long as you spend it before the step or phase ends.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?
